key_insight: Tree-Ising repairs reasoning loops through sparse BF16 weight edits, outperforming an LLM-agent repair without gradients or LLM tokens.
engineering_relevance: Discrete weight optimization offers a low-cost repair workflow using four forward-pass requests and about $0.90 in GPU time for the annealing recipe.
method: Use forward statistics to weaken looping, strengthen concluding, and preserve productive-token outputs.
Restrict edits to admissible sign flips and exponent shifts while preserving shared group exponents and mantissas.
Decompose the objective exactly into per-row QUBO problems solved with GPU simulated annealing or simulated bifurcation.
evidence_signal: On Qwen3.5-0.8B, Tree-Ising achieves 54.6–55.1% MATH-500 accuracy versus 51.7% for the agent edit; improvements on MATH-500 and GSM8K remain significant after multiple-comparison correction.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the reported Qwen models and math benchmarks; the eight-variable QAOA demonstration does not establish practical quantum advantage.
paper_title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
